what: Page transition without a curtain: the page itself goes in and out through a shaped hole. Clicking a link to another page shrinks the page to .9 scale (.9s power2.inOut) and closes it into a hole shaped as a triangle, diamond, arch or stairs (from a size covering the screen to .6 of the short side, .9s power1.out, geometric interpolation). It rotates 90° (.8s power2.in) and exits upward off screen from .4s (.8s power2.inOut). Behind it lies a plate in that shape’s color. The new page rises from below the screen at .9 scale·−90°·small hole (.8s starting at .4s) and stands at 1 scale at .95s (.45s). The hole opens until it covers the screen (.4s power1.in) while rotating to 0° (1s power2.out starting at .4s). A 2px ink line runs around the hole

options.shape: triangle · diamond · arch · stairs · cycle (default — next type on each slide, continues across the session)
options.speed: Speed multiplier, default 1 (2 is twice as fast, 0 switches instantly with no transition)
options.[data-fx-part=backdrop]: Panel laid down outside the hole (optional, shape and color class fx-paint-<Type> is attached)

from.where: shared.js page transition (Transitions — swup in parallel, old and new pages sit together on the same timeline)

note: The original overlaps old and new pages on one screen with the swup parallel plugin. The part is split into two halves, leaving (the clicked page) and entering (the opened page), so it also works on sites that open a new document. Sites using swup or barba read the site’s single shared.js. Shape size follows a 400-unit path based on the screen’s long side, and cover scales are triangle 3.4, rhombus 2.1, arch 3, stairs 4.6 × 1.04
